subject.title: Pause blocked background Claude CLI auth probes

question: Should one unclassified five-second Claude auth-status timeout suppress background Auto CLI checks for six hours, or must the long cooldown require repeated or stronger blocked-prompt evidence?
rationale: The timeout signal cannot distinguish the reported Keychain dialog from ordinary transient CLI slowness, so the chosen policy directly trades prompt suppression against existing background provider availability.

options.title: Require stronger evidence
options.body: Use a short initial backoff and apply the six-hour cooldown only after repeated timeouts or a more specific blocked-prompt signal.

options.title: Accept broad cooldown
options.body: Treat every timeout as prompt-equivalent and accept that transient delays can disable background Claude CLI availability for six hours.

options.title: Use short cooldown only
options.body: Keep coalescing but cap all unclassified timeout and failure cooldowns at a short interval until a reliable blocked-prompt signal exists.

recommendation.title: Require stronger evidence
recommendation.body: Use a short initial backoff and apply the six-hour cooldown only after repeated timeouts or a more specific blocked-prompt signal.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the best available decision owner for an intentional compatibility and provider-routing tradeoff.
